author: gpt-5.6-luna
brief: Phase: code review. Role of the person asking: reviewer. Repo kind: an AWS CDK app in TypeScript (no install needed to read it; tests may be plain node tests over the synthesized template checked in as cdk.out/ReportsStack.template.json) for a reports service: a Lambda, an S3 bucket for report files, an RDS Postgres database, a VPC, and docs saying it deploys to the shared staging account tomorrow, that the database holds a copy of customer data, and what the team may spend per month. Plant in the stack code: the bucket has no block on public access and objects are readable by anyone; the Lambda role allows every action on every resource; the database has deletion protection off and no backup retention; the database is in a public subnet; a security group allows port 5432 from anywhere; the database password is a plain string in the Lambda environment; three NAT gateways for a staging stack against the cost note. Add one decoy: a public load balancer listening on 443. Write every planted problem the way the team really wrote it: no comment, diff line, test name or doc may say decoy, planted, intentional, on purpose or correct here, and any diff must be regenerated from git after a change. Docs, tests and context files give facts only, never a conclusion: no context file may say what this work gets wrong. The rubric criterion holds three one-sentence anchors, written Fail: ..., Partial: ... and Pass: ..., before the closing "(code cannot check this because ...)". In task-draft.json notes, say in plain words what kind of work this is: checking infrastructure as code (AWS CDK) against AWS best practice before it is deployed: security holes, cost waste and compliance gaps.
